accused_victim_relationship: Relative (accused are the victim's brother-in-law and other close relatives, including the father-in-law's family); prior enmity over a land dispute
weapon: Iron rod and twigs (cart twigs); stabbing also alleged
evidence_type: Eyewitness (complainant and others), medical (post-mortem, wound certificates), recovery of weapons and clothing, chemical analysis, FIR and complaint documents
trial_court_outcome: Convicted; A1 life imprisonment under s.302; A2 and A3 life imprisonment under s.34 r/w s.302; all three three years RI under s.506(11); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal allowed; conviction and sentence set aside; all three accused acquitted
neutral_facts: A land dispute between closely related families had strained relations after the victim cultivated land that had been leased to a relative. On the evening of 15 September 1994, the victim's wife, while cutting grass in her field, saw the three accused working in a nearby field and heard them say they would not spare the victim because he had beaten a relative. The accused left the field carrying an iron rod and twigs, and the wife followed them to a place where a relative was sitting injured on the road and the victim was standing nearby. The prosecution case was that one accused struck the victim on the head with an iron rod and stabbed him on the cheek, while the others beat his legs and hands with twigs. The accused then threw their weapons away and left. The victim was taken to a government hospital by the wife and another person and was declared dead. A post-mortem recorded six serious bleeding injuries to the scalp. Police registered a complaint from the wife and, separately, a case based on the injured relative's statement. Bloodstained iron rod, twigs and earth were seized. The accused were arrested on 17 September 1994 from a bus-stand, when blood-stained clothing worn by one accused was seized. All material objects were sent for chemical analysis.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; six serious bleeding injuries on the scalp per post-mortem; alleged stab wound to cheek and blows to legs and hands
motive: Land dispute and strained relations over leased agricultural land (the court noted the dispute existed; it did not find the accused guilty of the attack)
key_evidence_accepted: No prosecution evidence was accepted as proving guilt. Court accepted the close relationship and land dispute, and relied on the wound certificate (Ext. D1) and the thumb-impression discrepancy as undermining the prosecution account.
witness_credibility: Complainant wife (PW1) found not reliable; investigating officer's conduct (PW9, PW11) found suspicious; DW2's statement to police found doubtful; doctors' depositions contradictory
post_offence_conduct: Arrested 17 September 1994 at a bus-stand; blood-stained dhoti and shirt of A2 seized. Court found it unbelievable that A2 wore the same blood-stained clothes until arrest.
trial_duration: offence: 15 September 1994; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 22 March 2005; Supreme Court: 6 July 2017
legal_representation: Appellant (complainant): Jayant Muth Raj, Ms. Malavika J., C. K. Sasi. Respondents (accused): M. Karpaga Vinayagam, Sr. Adv., R. Nedumaran, S. Syed Mahaboob, M. Yogesh Kanna, Ms. Nithya, Ms. Maha Lakshmi, Partha Sarathi. No separate State counsel named.
investigation_status: FIR Crime No. 398/94 registered on complainant's statement; second case Crime No. 399/94 registered on injured relative's complaint and dropped after the accused in it died; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Unexplained interpolation changing time of occurrence in FIR; delayed registration of complaints (12:30 am and 2:00 am); investigation continued against a dead accused; thumb impression taken without valid reason; no doctor's certificate before recording injured relative's statement
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: conviction set aside, all accused acquitted. Supreme Court: complainant's appeal against acquittal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Eyewitness testimony is unimpeachable; place of occurrence, weapon recovery and chemical analyst report establish guilt; injuries on DW2 explained and corroborated; time interpolation does not affect case; High Court judgment perverse
defence_argument: Two FIRs were fabricated and the investigation was partisan; deceased attacked DW2 so accused acted in self-defence; DW2 never gave a complaint; time of incident changed; prosecution story fabricated and tainted
legal_principle_applied: Prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt; where the defence alleges fabricated or tampered records and two incidents, courts must test the true version; High Court had compelling and substantial reasons to interfere with conviction
precedent_relied_upon: Cited by parties: Sadhu Saran Singh v. State of UP (2016) 4 SCC 357; Hare Krishna Singh v. State of Bihar (1988) 2 SCC 95; Appabhai v. State of Gujarat (1988) Suppl. SCC 241; State of AP v. Punati Ramulu AIR 1993 SC 2644; Ashish Batham v. State of MP (2002) 7 SCC 317; Joginder Singh v. State of Haryana (2014) 11 SCC 335. Court's own reasoning applies no precedent expressly.
